standard_full: ISO 8733:1997 (parallel pins with internal thread, of unhardened steel and austenitic stainless steel; = DIN EN ISO 8733:1998). Not the withdrawn DIN 7979 table. The hardened pin (ISO 8735:1997) is not covered by this table.
scope: 비경화형(ISO 8733) 치수만 — 경화형(ISO 8735)의 모따기 a·c와 길이 범위는 싣지 않았습니다 (경화형의 나사·구멍 치수가 같다는 것은 공개 자료 3곳 이상으로 확인하지 못했습니다)

shape_hint: Cylindrical dowel pin (m6) with a tapped blind hole in one end for an extraction screw: thread d2 with full thread depth t1, drilled depth t2, and a short counterbore d3 x t3 at the entry. The threaded end has a small chamfer (a / c1); the hardened pin (ISO 8735) has a crowned opposite end, the unhardened pin (ISO 8733) a chamfer at both ends.

role_map.d2: internal thread, metric coarse thread size (pages print M4 ... M24; stored as the number)
role_map.d3: diameter of the counterbore at the thread entry
role_map.t2_min: depth of the drilled hole, minimum
role_map.c1_unhard: chamfer at the threaded end (ISO 8733 symbol c1, approximate; globalfastener calls it a)

notes: Verified record narrowed to one standard: ISO 8733 (unhardened), 10 rows x 7 columns. The researcher's table pooled pages of ISO 8733 and ISO 8735; counted per standard, the hardened-pin pages give only 2 clusters for d3, t3 and the thread of d 6 / d 8. d2 is stored as the thread's nominal diameter because the record format takes numbers only; the column label says 4 = M4. Symbol mapping was checked on each page's drawing: globalfastener (d_1 thread, d_2 counterbore, a at the threaded end), fasten.it (c3 thread depth, c4 hole depth, c1 at the threaded end), fasteners.eu (standard symbols). fasteners.eu prints t2 without the word min.

verification.checks_done: All pages re-downloaded by the verifier with curl (browser User-Agent) on 2026-11-11 into a separate directory (HTTP 200, text/html); tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (html.parser grid with rowspan/colspan), not the researcher's scripts or raw files. Pages: globalfastener detail_257 (ISO 8733) + detail_266 (ISO 8735), fasten.it din_en_iso_8733 + din_en_iso_8735, fasteners.eu ISO/8733 (+ ISO/8735 = DIN/7979), opac producto-170, fastenerdata iso8735b, dm-muehl 8735_c1, schrauben-lexikon ISO_8735, boltport iso-8735 + iso-8733, ferrofast iso-8735, theo-schrauben DIN-7979; the dimension drawings of globalfastener (both pages), fasten.it (both pages), fasteners.eu and dm-muehl were opened to see what each letter marks. Counted three ways: pooled as the researcher did (min 3), ISO 8735 pages alone (min 2), ISO 8733 pages alone (min 3) - the last is the kept table.
problems: Table narrowed to ISO 8733. Per standard, the hardened pin (ISO 8735) has: d3 and t3 on 2 clusters (globalfastener, fastenerdata), thread size of d 6 and d 8 on 2 (globalfastener, fasten.it; fastenerdata prints M3 / M4), t1 / t2 / a on 3. A table titled 'ISO 8735 · ISO 8733' would therefore claim hardened-pin values that only two sources print. If the lead accepts pooling the two sibling standards, the researcher's 10 x 8 table is numerically intact with a minimum of 3 pooled clusters (a_hard exactly 3: globalfastener, fasten.it, fastenerdata).
dm-muehl 'ISO 8735 C1' page removed from the count: it is the dealer's DIN 7979 sheet under an ISO title (the researcher had counted it for a and d2 of d 6-12).

fasten.it's c3 / c4 are the thread depth and hole depth by its own drawing; the researcher left them out as 'site symbols'. Read that way, the fasten.it ISO 8733 page dissents on thread depth for d 12 / 16 / 20 (10 / 12 / 16, the DIN 7979 numbers) against 12 / 16 / 18 on globalfastener, fasteners.eu and OPAC (and on all three ISO 8735 pages). Those three cells stand on exactly 3 clusters with one dissenting page.
d2: thread size is printed as M-designation on all four counted pages; label changed to say that 4 means M4.

Letters taken from drawings: globalfastener's d_2 (= counterbore) and a (= threaded-end chamfer) are fixed by its drawing, which shows them there; without globalfastener c1 still has 3 clusters, but d3 and t3 need it (fasteners.eu and OPAC print d3 / t3 by name).

Not counted, for the lead's information: the publisher-authorised preview service (standards.iteh.ai sample PDF, a T1-type source under app/SOURCE_RULE.md) shows the dimension table of this ISO standard; the kept values equal it. The table could be re-based on that official preview instead of T2. (ISO 8733:1997 preview Table 1: c1, c2, d2, P, d3, t1, t2 min, t3 for d1 6-50, equal to the record incl. t1 12 / 16 / 18. The ISO 8735:1997 preview shows the same d2, d3, t1, t2, t3, a ≈ 0.8 ... 6.3 and c 2.1 / 2.6 / 3 / 3.8 / 4.6 / 6 / 6 / 7 / 8 / 10 - so the full hardened + unhardened table is available on the T1 route.)
